subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs (Acme)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-28T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs (Acme)

Jordan / Samantha — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth. High-level takeaways: 

Pain points / goals
- Current in-house solution is missing 95th percentile latency targets during peak usage (user-facing chat)
- Need predictable per-request latency for short prompts (~50-150 tokens) and throughput for batch scoring jobs
- Want ability to failover to lower-cost model variant during spikes without impacting availability

Technical requirements you called out
- Latency target: P95 <= 150 ms for short prompts (<= 150 tokens)
- Burst throughput: up to 120 QPS sustained for 5-10 minute windows; baseline expected ~20 QPS
- Model: production-gen LLM (approx 7B-13B range) for chat; separate embedding model for search rerank
- Deployment topology: prefer Dedicated capacity in us-west with option for Private VPC for sensitive traffic

Notes on constraints
- Must retain audit logs for 90 days (compliance)
- Key management via Acme KMS (customer-managed keys)

Attachments included: acme-slo-proposal.pdf (summary of SLOs and recommended config), redwood-deployment-topology.png (proposed network topology), acme-kpis.xlsx (sample KPIs you shared)

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood to share detailed perf estimate (latency/throughput) by model variant + recommended GPU profile — deliver by Mon, Mar 2
2) Schedule infra deep-dive with Acme Ops to validate VPC/network and KMS integration — propose Tue, Mar 3 or Wed, Mar 4
3) Acme to confirm acceptance criteria for regression (quality) and any internal SLA requirements

If I missed anything or misstated a requirement, please reply with corrections. Otherwise we’ll proceed with the perf estimate and lock a time for the infra call.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-28T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs (Acme)

Thanks Aditya — this looks accurate. Couple clarifications: 
- The 120 QPS burst number is for the public chat endpoint (mix of short prompts). For batch reranking (embeddings) we expect up to 300 concurrent requests but those are background and can tolerate higher latency (P95 <= 2s).
- For the chat model we plan to use a 1-2 second context window on average, so KV cache behavior and per-token latency matter.

A question for Redwood: what model variants do you recommend for hitting P95 150ms on 7B-13B parameter models? Also, what GPU types would you size for Dedicated capacity to support the 120 QPS bursts with a 99.9% availability SLO?

Jordan
Jordan Miller
Head of Product, Acme Corp
jordan.miller@acme.com
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>
Cc: ops-team@acme.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-01T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs (Acme)

Agree with Jordan — additional details from our side: 
- Target for chat: P50 <= 40 ms, P95 <= 150 ms, tail (P99) we'd like < 300 ms if possible
- We have regulatory requirement to keep request/response logs for 90 days and redact PII in logs before export
- For failover, we'd accept a lower-quality distilled model with identical API surface (no schema changes)

Also: could you include a rough cost delta between hosted vs dedicated for our baseline QPS? We want to present cost options to finance.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Corp
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: sizing proposal for Acme (draft)

Forwarding the thread for context — drafting a Dedicated sizing recommendation. Initial thoughts: 
- For 7B-13B chat model to meet P95 150ms at 120 QPS bursts we should recommend a pool of A100/80GB-class GPUs with sharded serving and aggressive prefix caching. Expect 4-8 GPUs in the Dedicated pool depending on batching.
- For embeddings / rerank: cheaper T4/RTX-class capacity with autoscaling to handle 300 concurrent background jobs.
- Propose optional Private VPC deployment for their sensitive traffic and KMS integration.

Action items for us: get perf numbers from runtime team (Aditya), draft cost comparison hosted vs dedicated (Monica). I’ll draft the FAQ for the infra call.

— Lauren
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, ops-team@acme.com
Date: 2026-03-02T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs (Acme)

Appreciate the quick clarifications. Next steps and owners: 
1) Redwood perf estimate (by model variant + GPU profile) — owner: Aditya — deliverable: PDF with latency/throughput table and recommended config — due: Mon, Mar 2 EOD (attached: acme-slo-proposal.pdf)
2) Cost comparison (hosted vs dedicated) — owner: Monica — deliverable: spreadsheet — due: Tue, Mar 3 — (attached: acme-kpis.xlsx sample; Monica will share the full table)
3) Infra deep-dive (VPC/KMS/network) — owner: Acme Ops + Redwood infra — proposed times: Tue, Mar 3 10:00 AM PST or Wed, Mar 4 11:00 AM PST — please confirm preferred slot
4) Confirmation of acceptance criteria for quality/regression and any compliance docs required — owner: Acme (Jordan/Samantha) — please provide by Fri, Mar 6

I’ve attached the deployment topology diagram (redwood-deployment-topology.png) and the SLO proposal. If those look good we’ll use them as the base for the infra call.

If you’re good with the proposed times I’ll send a calendar invite and include our infra/ops lead.

— Aditya
